summary: Add explicit negotiated semantic transcript projection, native source-linked categories and usage facts, relay support and projection-revision fencing. Existing UI clients remain on their current capability by default.

replay.detail: Derived native timeline folds rebuild when normalization revision changes and obsolete semantic cursors require resync. Native transcript bytes, identities and durable claim history are not rewritten.

schema.detail: No database or storage version change. Optional wire fields are described under compatibility.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or fleet coordination changes.

compatibility.detail: conversation-semantics.v1 requires conversation-blocks.v1 and compatible owner/relay support. Unsupported semantic versions are refused. Opted-in responses carry source-linked semantic blocks and header projection revision, omit raw-as-prose fallbacks and legacy summed header cost. Unnegotiated clients retain their existing wire bodies and cursor shape; no first-party UI automatically opts in.

downtime.detail: No additional service interruption or data migration is required beyond ordinary binary rollout; no timing measurement is claimed.

manual.detail: Existing clients require no manual action. Explicit semantic consumers must support the negotiated revision and resync expired cursors.

recovery.detail: Native records remain authoritative. Older owners reject semantic opt-in; supported legacy-capability clients remain usable after rollback, and semantic cursors may require resync.
